pages.lesson:
LESSON: AREA

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements
Topic 3.1: Area

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Area
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How is area different from perimeter?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. explain area as the space covered by a flat shape
2. find area of a rectangle using length × width
3. find area of a square using side × side
4. use square centimetres (cm²) or square metres (m²)

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ What is area?

• Area is the amount of flat space a shape covers.
• We measure area in cm² or m².

▸ Area of a rectangle

Teach
• Area = Length × Width.
• Both sides must use the same unit first.

Worked example
• A book cover is 18 cm by 13 cm.
• Area = 18 × 13.
• 18 × 10 = 180, 18 × 3 = 54, total 234.
• Area = 234 cm².

Try this
• Rectangle 10 cm by 7 cm. Find area.
• Classroom floor 9 m by 6 m. Find area.
• (Check later: 70 cm²; 54 m²)

▸ Area of a square

Teach
• Area = side × side.

Worked example
• Square tile side 15 cm → Area = 15 × 15 = 225 cm².

Try this
• Square side 8 cm. Find area.
• Square garden side 5 m. Find area.
• (Check later: 64 cm²; 25 m²)


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• 18 × 13 = 234 cm²
• 15 × 15 = 225 cm²
• 9 × 6 = 54 m²

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Find area: 12 cm by 5 cm rectangle.
2. Find area: square side 9 cm.
3. Word problem: A rectangular plot is 20 m by 15 m. Find its area.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Measure a book and calculate its area.
2. Draw 2 shapes, label sides, find area.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is area different from perimeter?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Area = space covered.
• Rectangle: L × W.
• Square: side × side.
• Use cm² or m².

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
